variants.title: Boyle's law: air trapped at 100 mL in a 15 °C winter laboratory
variants.sample: Air, trapped at 100 mL and 101.3 kPa
variants.note: n = P V / (R T) = 101325 x 1e-4 / (8.314 x 288.15) = 4.23 mmol. PV is 10.13 J, the same as the trapped air started with.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part 2, Class XI, Ch. 12 Kinetic Theory (Boyle's law, PV = nRT, R = 8.314 J/(mol K))
source.note: Condition: room at 15 °C, standard atmosphere 101.325 kPa.

variants.title: Boyle's law: air trapped at 100 mL in a 35 °C summer laboratory
variants.sample: Air, trapped at 100 mL and 101.3 kPa
variants.note: Warmer air: fewer moles fill the same 100 mL at room pressure (n = 3.96 mmol), yet PV is again 10.13 J.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part 2, Class XI, Ch. 12 Kinetic Theory (Boyle's law, PV = nRT)
source.note: Condition: room at 35 °C, standard atmosphere 101.325 kPa.

variants.title: Boyle's law: a small sample of air, trapped at 50 mL
variants.sample: Air, trapped at 50 mL and 101.3 kPa
variants.note: Half the gas: PV = 5.07 J, and the pressure stays low enough to pull the plunger out to 200 mL (about 25 kPa).

source.title: NCERT Physics Part 2, Class XI, Ch. 12 Kinetic Theory (Boyle's law, PV = nRT)

variants.title: Boyle's law: a large sample of air, trapped at 150 mL
variants.sample: Air, trapped at 150 mL and 101.3 kPa
variants.note: More gas: PV = 15.2 J. The gauge reaches its 600 kPa limit sooner, so the smallest volume is 30 mL.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part 2, Class XI, Ch. 12 Kinetic Theory (Boyle's law, PV = nRT)

variants.title: Boyle's law in a hill-station laboratory at 2,200 m (as at Shimla)
variants.sample: Air, trapped at 100 mL and 77.5 kPa
variants.note: The room pressure at 2,200 m in the standard atmosphere is 77.5 kPa, so the trapped air holds fewer moles: PV = 7.75 J.

source.title: ICAO Standard Atmosphere (ISO 2533): p = 101325 (1 - 2.25577e-5 h)^5.25588 Pa; p(2200 m) = 77.54 kPa

variants.title: Boyle's law in a high-altitude laboratory at 3,500 m (as at Leh)
variants.sample: Air, trapped at 100 mL and 65.8 kPa
variants.note: At 3,500 m the standard-atmosphere pressure is 65.8 kPa: the gauge starts well below 100 kPa and PV = 6.58 J.

source.title: ICAO Standard Atmosphere (ISO 2533): p = 101325 (1 - 2.25577e-5 h)^5.25588 Pa; p(3500 m) = 65.76 kPa
